capabilities: browse the web in tabs with history, bookmarks, a reading list, and a Bing-style search shell
extract articles with Readability and convert them to editable Markdown notes via Turndown
save pages as HTML or MHTML and download URLs into a configured vault folder
run URL-matched user CSS and JavaScript rules, translate pages, and read page text aloud
expose a versioned API so other plugins like Cancip can read the current page and control tabs
extras: Manual install by copying files into the vault; listed as not manually reviewed by Obsidian staff; the rendered-DOM extraction pass only works on desktop Electron, while mobile falls back to fetch-only extraction (README notes this platform limit).
intentEvidence: NoteDraw buttons are deduped so Mobile Webviewer surfaces keep one visible magic-wand launcher while still using NoteDraw's real page controller behind it.
motivation: NoteWeb "is meant to be the best Markdown view of a web page you can get inside Obsidian."
problem: Obsidian has no strong built-in way to browse the web, especially on mobile, or to capture pages as readable, editable Markdown notes.

relations.evidence: still using NoteDraw's real page controller behind it
Cancip uses this API before falling back to generic plugin commands or a second network fetch

summary: Mobile-first in-app web browser with tabs, history, bookmarks, downloads, and a Readability-based reader mode that saves pages as editable Markdown notes.
